wps.title_source_en: Work Package 2: Preliminary diagnosis, feedstock qualification and circular framework design
wps.title_es: Diagnóstico preliminar, cualificación de materias primas y diseño del marco circular
wps.objective_source_en:
WP2 will establish the technical and circular basis required to transform heterogeneous, currently under-valorised complex plastic waste streams into stable secondary materials for high-value applications. Its specific objectives are to:
Define the quantified technical, environmental, economic and market baseline, including reference scenarios and the preliminary LIFE KPI framework.
Characterise and qualify the target complex waste streams in terms of composition, contaminants, variability, availability, recycling potential and suitability for the planned applications.
Define standardisable pre-treatment and conditioning routes able to convert heterogeneous input materials into stable, continuous and reliable material streams.
Establish the application-specific material and product requirements for recycled boards and recovered polyolefin applications.
Design the advanced valorisation concept and the closed-Ciclo framework needed to guide WP3 (upscaling), WP4 (traceability/return-Ciclo design) and WP5 (demonstrations).
WP2 will deliver the validated baseline, KPI framework and feedstock qualification required to reduce technical uncertainty before pre-industrial implementation. It will define the conditioning and valorisation routes needed to transform non-valorised or low-value waste into stable, high-value secondary materials conceived for concrete applications. The WP will also provide the application requirements and circular design principles that will guide subsequent upscaling, traceability, demonstration and impact assessment activities.
wps.objective_es:
WP2 establecerá la base técnica y circular necesaria para transformar corrientes heterogéneas de residuos plásticos complejos actualmente infravalorizadas en materiales secundarios estables para aplicaciones de alto valor. Sus objetivos específicos son: Definir la base técnica, ambiental, económica y de mercado cuantificada, incluyendo escenarios de referencia y el marco preliminar de LIFE KPI.
Caracterizar y clasificar las corrientes de residuos complejas en términos de composición, contaminantes, variabilidad, disponibilidad, potencial de reciclaje y idoneidad para las aplicaciones planificadas. Definir las rutas pretratamiento y condicionamiento estandarizables capaces de convertir materiales de entrada heterogénea en corrientes de materiales estables, continuas y fiables.
Establecer los requisitos de materiales y productos específicos para aplicaciones de tableros reciclados y aplicaciones de poliolefina recuperadas. Diseñar el concepto de valorización avanzada y el marco de cierre necesario para guiar WP3 (escalado), WP4 (trazabilidad/diseño del circuito de retorno) y WP5 (demostraciones).
WP2 entregará la base validada, el marco KPI y la calificación de materia prima requerida para reducir la incertidumbre técnica antes de la implementación preindustrial. Definirá las rutas de condicionamiento y valorización necesarias para transformar los residuos no validados o de bajo valor en materiales secundarios estables y de alto valor concebidos para aplicaciones concretas.
El Programa también proporcionará los requisitos de aplicación y los principios de diseño circular que guiarán las actividades posteriores de aumento, trazabilidad, demostración y evaluación de impacto.

ITENE; Participants: CABKA, CEV, EDRO, MANC, MUN, PP) (M4-M9):
This task will define the material families, performance requirements and application criteria for the project’s target products. The task will ensure that the materials developed in the project are not generic recycled outputs, but secondary raw materials designed for concrete applications with clear technical, operational and market requirements.
ITENE will lead the definition of the requirements framework, building on the feedstock characterisation results from T2.2 and the purification and conditioning routes defined in T2.3. The work will first assess the feasibility of each material fraction, considering its measured properties, achievable purification level, critical limitations, potential need for blending and scalability of the sorting and conditioning process. This assessment will be carried out from an industrial perspective, ensuring that the expected material qualities are realistic and compatible with pre-industrial implementation. A decision matrix will then be developed to link each fraction with the most suitable valorisation route and target application. The matrix will consider critical material parameters, achievable qualities, purification capacity, processability and added-value potential, supporting decisions on whether each material should be directed to pressing, board production, injection moulding, packaging applications or other suitable routes. It will also assess the convenience of blending different fractions to enhance complementary properties or compensate for individual weaknesses. MANC will provide industrial criteria related to recycling feasibility, material preparation, process stability and recycled board applications. PP will contribute requirements for transformation into boards and demonstrator products, including processability, formulation and performance needs. CABKA will define the requirements for recovered polyolefins in reusable packaging and logistics applications, including material quality, durability, processability and reuse conditions. EDRO and MUN will provide end-user and operational requirements for construction, municipal infrastructure, public equipment and real deployment environments, including installation, use, maintenance, acceptance and recovery considerations. CEV will contribute market and buyer-related requirements, including acceptance barriers, green procurement potential and value-chain expectations.
The task will generate a standardised knowledge framework and decision-support tool to assign viable valorisation routes to complex waste fractions, including those with no clear commercial outlet at the starting point. This framework will support industrial decision-making, future replication and the development of standardisable criteria based on scientific evidence and real material properties. The results of this task will support MS4 and will feed D2.3

KIWA; Participants: CABKA, CEV, EDRO, ITENE, MANC, MUN, PP) (M6-M9):
This task will define the circular design rules for each closed loop, ensuring that the materials and products developed in the project are conceived from the outset for traceability, reuse, repair, return, recycling and reintegration into the value chain. The task will connect the material and application requirements defined in T2.4 with the operational return-loop protocols and digital traceability architecture to be developed in WP4.
KIWA will lead the definition of the closed-loop design framework, identifying the traceability, verification and data requirements needed to follow materials, batches and product units across production, use, return and reintegration stages. This will include the preliminary definition of product identification needs, data capture points, recycled content evidence, return-event records and links with future Digital Product Passport and circularity verification activities. ITENE will contribute technical and environmental criteria related to recyclability, material quality, circularity indicators and impact monitoring needs. MANC and PP will provide industrial input on processing feasibility, product design constraints, repairability, reprocessing and reintegration of recovered materials into new production cycles. EDRO and MUN will contribute operational requirements, including installation, use conditions, maintenance, return feasibility and acceptance by public or private end users. CABKA will define return, reuse and pool-management needs for the reusable packaging loop, including logistics performance, product identification and end-of-life reintegration. CEV will provide input on buyer expectations, green public procurement potential, market acceptance and replication conditions.
The task will define specific circular design rules for each application, covering product design principles, material compatibility, recyclability, repairability, durability, return conditions, inspection criteria, traceability needs and reintegration routes. It will also identify the information that must be captured during production and use to support the WP4 return-loop protocols, traceability system and circularity verification methodology. The results of this task will complete the WP2 circular framework and ensure that the subsequent technical and demonstration activities are aligned with closed-loop principles. They will support MS4 and will be included in D2.3.

wps.title_source_en: Work Package 3: Pre-industrial upscaling of the advanced valorisation system and production of demonstration material batches
wps.title_es: Escalado preindustrial y producción de lotes de material para demostración
wps.objective_source_en:
WP3 will implement, validate and optimise at pre-industrial scale the advanced valorisation system designed in WP2, demonstrating its capacity to transform complex and difficult-to-recycle plastic waste into high-quality recycled raw materials for the R-Mob TraceLoop applications. Its specific objectives are to:
Install, integrate and commission the advanced valorisation system in an industrially relevant environment.
Transfer the technical specifications defined in WP2 into a robust and operational pre-industrial process.
Optimise process parameters and material formulations for the selected waste streams and target applications.
Produce homogeneous, reproducible and application-specific recycled material batches for the WP5 demonstrators.
Validate the quality, stability, processability and technical performance of the produced materials against the requirements defined in WP2.
Define and implement batch identification and production data requirements to support integration with the traceability system developed in WP4.
Generate pre-industrial evidence on the technical feasibility, industrial robustness, scalability and replication potential of the R-Mob TraceLoop valorisation model.
WP3 will deliver a fully commissioned and operational advanced valorisation system, together with validated operating protocols and optimised process conditions for the selected complex plastic waste streams. The work package will produce application-specific recycled material batches for the selected applications. These batches will be quality-controlled, technically validated, identified and prepared for the closed-Ciclo demonstrations in WP5. WP3 will also generate the pre-industrial evidence needed to demonstrate process stability, material reproducibility, traceability preparación and the future scalability of the valorisation model.
wps.objective_es:
WP3 implementará, validará y optimizará a escala preindustrial el sistema avanzado de valorización diseñado en WP2, demostrando su capacidad para transformar residuos plásticos complejos y difíciles de reciclar en materias primas recicladas de alta calidad para las aplicaciones R-Mob TraceLoop. Sus objetivos específicos son:
Instalar, integrar y encargar el sistema avanzado de valorización en un entorno industrialmente relevante. Transferir las especificaciones técnicas definidas en WP2 en un proceso preindustrial robusto y operativo. Optimizar los parámetros de proceso y formulaciones materiales para las secuencias de residuos seleccionadas y aplicaciones de destino.
Producir lotes de material reciclado homogéneo, reproducible y específico para aplicaciones para los demostradores WP5. Validar la calidad, estabilidad, procesabilidad y rendimiento técnico de los materiales producidos contra los requisitos definidos en WP2. Defina e implemente requisitos de identificación y producción de lotes para apoyar la integración con el sistema de trazabilidad desarrollado en WP4.
Generar evidencia preindustrial sobre la viabilidad técnica, robustez industrial, escalabilidad y potencial de replicación del modelo de valorización R-Mob TraceLoop.
WP3 ofrecerá un sistema de valorización avanzada totalmente encargado y operativo, junto con protocolos operativos validados y condiciones de proceso optimizadas para las corrientes de residuos plásticos complejas seleccionadas. El paquete de trabajo producirá lotes de materiales reciclados específicos para aplicaciones seleccionadas.
Estos lotes serán controlados por la calidad, validados técnicamente, identificados y preparados para las demostraciones de cierre en WP5. WP3 también generará las pruebas preindustriales necesarias para demostrar estabilidad de procesos, reproducibilidad material, preparación de trazabilidad y la escalabilidad futura del modelo de valorización.

PP; Participants: CABKA, EDRO, ITENE, MANC) (M13-M24):
This task will produce the application-specific material batches required for the LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop demonstrators, using the process conditions and formulations optimised in T3.2. The objective is to ensure the availability of sufficient, representative and reproducible recycled materials for subsequent demonstrator manufacturing, functional validation and replication activities.
MANC will operate Module 1 and the integrated valorisation process to produce the recycled material outputs under the validated process conditions. It will ensure operational control, monitor production parameters, identify deviations and verify that the process remains stable and repeatable across production campaigns. PP will ensure that the formulations and downstream transformation requirements for Module 2 are maintained during production, so that the generated material is suitable for board and demonstrator manufacturing. ITENE will technically characterise the materials produced during the different campaigns, assessing their quality, consistency and suitability against the requirements defined in WP2. EDRO will validate the suitability of the relevant batches for construction-related applications, considering functional, operational and installation requirements. CABKA will assess the adequacy of recovered polyolefin batches for reusable packaging and logistics applications, providing additional requirements or adjustments when necessary.
PP will coordinate the batch production strategy, defining the production campaigns, material allocation, target quantities, formulation control and logistics required to supply the different application routes. The task will cover recycled material batches for furniture, construction and reusable packaging. The estimated production volumes will be defined according to the needs of the WP5 demonstrators and will include approximately XXX kg of recycled compounds and/or boards for the furniture and public/interior equipment demonstrators, XXX kg/t of recycled materials and/or boards for construction or municipal infrastructure applications, and XXX kg of recovered polyolefin compounds for reusable packaging and logistics-related validation. These quantities will be refined during campaign planning, taking into account demonstrator design, manufacturing yields, testing needs, quality control samples, contingency margins and material requirements for possible replication or additional validation activities.
The task will follow a staged production approach, starting with campaign planning and definition of quantities, followed by continuous or semi-continuous batch production, operational monitoring and verification of repeatability between campaigns. For each production campaign, the consortium will record the target quantity, actual quantity produced, material losses, rejected fraction, quantity released for demonstrator manufacturing, quantity reserved for testing and quality control, and quantity available for contingency or additional validation. The final stage will focus on the review and release of the produced batches for characterisation, identification, demonstrator manufacturing and validation in WP5.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have produced and released representative application-specific material batches with sufficient quantity, quality and traceability readiness to support the closed-loop demonstrations. The results of this task will contribute to MS7 and will feed D3.3.

PP; Participantes: CABKA, EDRO, ITENE, MANC) (M13-M24):
Esta tarea producirá los lotes de material específicos para la aplicación requeridos para los demostradores LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop, utilizando las condiciones de proceso y formulaciones optimizadas en T3.2. El objetivo es garantizar la disponibilidad de materiales reciclados suficientes, representativos y reproducibles para actividades de fabricación, validación funcional y replicación de los demostradores posteriores.
MANC operará el Módulo 1 y el proceso de valorización integrada para producir los productos de materiales reciclados en las condiciones de proceso validados. Garantizará el control operativo, supervisará los parámetros de producción, identificará las desviaciones y verificará que el proceso sigue siendo estable y repetible en las campañas de producción.
PP se asegurará de que las formulaciones y requisitos de transformación de abajo para el Módulo 2 se mantengan durante la producción, de modo que el material generado sea adecuado para la fabricación de tableros y demostradores. ITENE caracterizará técnicamente los materiales producidos durante las diferentes campañas, evaluando su calidad, consistencia y idoneidad frente a los requisitos definidos en WP2.
EDRO validará la idoneidad de los lotes pertinentes para aplicaciones relacionadas con la construcción, considerando los requisitos funcionales, operativos y de instalación. CABKA evaluará la idoneidad de lotes recuperados de poliolefina para aplicaciones de embalaje y logística reutilizables, proporcionando requisitos o ajustes adicionales cuando sea necesario.
PP coordinará la estrategia de producción de lotes, definiendo las campañas de producción, asignación de materiales, cantidades objetivo, control de formulación y logística necesarias para abastecer las diferentes rutas de aplicación. La tarea cubrirá lotes de material reciclado para muebles, construcción y embalaje reutilizable.
Los volúmenes de producción estimados se definirán según las necesidades de los demostradores WP5 y incluirán aproximadamente XXX kg de compuestos y/o tableros reciclados para los muebles y demostradores de equipo público/interior, XXX kg/t de materiales reciclados y/o tableros para aplicaciones de construcción o infraestructura municipal, y XXX kg de compuestos de poliolefina recuperados para embalaje reutilizable y validación logística relacionada.
Estas cantidades se refinarán durante la planificación de campañas, teniendo en cuenta el diseño de los demostradores, los rendimientos de fabricación, las necesidades de pruebas, las muestras de control de calidad, los márgenes de contingencia y los requisitos materiales para posibles actividades de replicación o validación adicional.
La tarea seguirá un enfoque de producción escalonada, comenzando por la planificación de campañas y la definición de cantidades, seguida de la producción continua o semicontinua de lotes, el seguimiento operacional y la verificación de la repetición entre las campañas.
Para cada campaña de producción, el consorcio registrará la cantidad de destino, la cantidad real producida, las pérdidas materiales, la fracción rechazada, la cantidad liberada para la fabricación de demostradores, la cantidad reservada para pruebas y control de calidad, y la cantidad disponible para contingencia o validación adicional.
La etapa final se centrará en la revisión y liberación de los lotes producidos para caracterización, identificación, fabricación y validación de demostradores en WP5.
Al final de la tarea, el consorcio habrá producido y liberado lotes de material representativos para aplicaciones con suficiente cantidad, calidad y preparación para la trazabilidad para apoyar las demostraciones de ciclo cerrado. Los resultados de esta tarea contribuirán a MS7 y alimentarán a D3.3.

ITENE, Participants: CABKA, EDRO, KIWA, MANC, PP) (M20-M25):
This task will verify that the recycled materials produced in T3.3 meet the technical, functional and quality requirements defined for the project demonstrators. It will confirm the stability of the pre-industrial production process, assess the conformity and consistency of the produced batches, and release the materials for their use in the WP5.
ITENE will lead the technical validation work, defining the characterisation plan, sampling approach, tests to be performed and acceptance criteria for each material family and application. The validation will include the assessment of relevant physical, mechanical, processing and functional properties, as well as dimensional stability, batch homogeneity and repeatability between production campaigns. The results will be compared with the application-specific requirements defined in WP2 to determine whether each batch is suitable for demonstration. MANC will provide the produced batches, process information and operational records needed to interpret the quality control results from an industrial perspective. PP will assess processability and verify that the materials are suitable for transformation into boards or other demonstrator products in Module 2. EDRO will contribute to the validation of the materials intended for construction, municipal infrastructure, furniture and public/interior equipment applications, considering functional and deployment-related requirements. CABKA will assess the suitability of recovered polyolefin materials for reusable packaging and logistics applications in Module 3. KIWA will support the batch traceability component, ensuring that the information generated during production and quality control is structured in a way that can feed the traceability architecture, Digital Product Passport and circularity verification activities developed in WP4. This will include batch identification data, production references, material origin, recycled content evidence, quality control results and release status.
The task will follow a progressive validation approach, starting with the definition of the testing and sampling plan, followed by technical characterisation, functional validation and final batch release. If deviations are detected, ITENE and the relevant technical partners will propose corrective adjustments before the batches are released for demonstration. The batch identification protocol will also consider the traceability principles of UNE-EN 15343, ensuring that relevant information on waste origin, recycled raw material, formulation, processing steps, quality controls and recycled content can be maintained when materials are further transformed, compounded or incorporated into boards, components and final products. By the end of the task, the consortium will have technically validated and released the pre-industrial material batches, with the necessary quality control evidence and traceability information to support their use in WP5 and their inclusion in the WP6 impact assessment. The results of this task will contribute to MS7 and will feed D3.3.

ITENE, Participantes: CABKA, EDRO, KIWA, MANC, PP) (M20-M25): Esta tarea verificará que los materiales reciclados producidos en T3.3 cumplan los requisitos técnicos, funcionales y de calidad definidos para los demostradores del proyecto. Confirmará la estabilidad del proceso de producción preindustrial, evaluará la conformidad y consistencia de los lotes producidos, y liberará los materiales para su uso en el WP5.
ITENE liderará el trabajo de validación técnica, definiendo el plan de caracterización, enfoque de muestreo, pruebas que se realizarán y criterios de aceptación para cada familia y aplicación material. La validación incluirá la evaluación de las propiedades físicas, mecánicas, de procesamiento y funcionales relevantes, así como la estabilidad dimensional, la homogeneidad de lotes y la repetibilidad entre las campañas de producción.
Los resultados se compararán con los requisitos específicos de aplicación definidos en WP2 para determinar si cada lote es adecuado para la demostración. MANC proporcionará los lotes producidos, información de proceso y registros operativos necesarios para interpretar los resultados de control de calidad desde una perspectiva industrial.
PP evaluará la procesabilidad y verificará que los materiales son adecuados para la transformación en tableros u otros productos de demostración en el Módulo 2. EDRO contribuirá a la validación de los materiales destinados a la construcción, infraestructura municipal, mobiliario y aplicaciones de equipo público/interior, teniendo en cuenta los requisitos funcionales y relacionados con el despliegue.
CABKA evaluará la idoneidad de los materiales recuperados de poliolefina para aplicaciones de embalaje reutilizables y logística en el Módulo 3. EDRO definirá la estructura de enlace con la trazabilidad conjunta: identificadores de lote, referencias de producción, origen material, evidencia de contenido reciclado, resultados de control de calidad y estado de liberación. KIWA revisará la auditabilidad y suficiencia de esa evidencia para las puertas de conformidad, sin diseñar la identidad, el DPP ni la arquitectura de trazabilidad.
La tarea seguirá un enfoque de validación progresiva, comenzando por la definición del plan de prueba y muestreo, seguido de caracterización técnica, validación funcional y liberación final de lotes. Si se detectan desviaciones, ITENE y los socios técnicos pertinentes propondrán ajustes correctivos antes de que los lotes sean liberados para la demostración.
El protocolo de identificación de lotes también examinará los principios de trazabilidad de la UNE-EN 15343, asegurando que se pueda mantener la información pertinente sobre el origen de los residuos, la materia prima reciclada, la formulación, las etapas de procesamiento, los controles de calidad y el contenido reciclado cuando se transformen, se compongan o incorporen más materiales en tableros, componentes y productos finales.
Al final de la tarea, el consorcio habrá validado técnicamente y liberado los lotes de material preindustrial, con la evidencia necesaria de control de calidad e información de trazabilidad para apoyar su uso en WP5 y su inclusión en la evaluación de impacto WP6. Los resultados de esta tarea contribuirán a MS7 y alimentarán D3.3.

KIWA; Participants: CABKA, EDRO, ITENE, MANC, MUN, PP) (M24-M28):
This task will ensure the correct identification of the material batches produced during pre-industrial scale-up and will prepare the industrial information required for their integration into the digital traceability system developed in WP4. The task will not develop the digital traceability platform itself, but will define and validate the production-level identification model, data structure and minimum information needed to ensure continuity of information across the value chain.
KIWA will lead the definition of the batch identification approach, including coding criteria, minimum data requirements, data capture points, production records, material-batch links and quality control references. The work will ensure that the information generated during WP3 can later feed the Data Space architecture, Digital Product Passport and circularity verification activities developed in WP4. MANC will record the industrial information generated during Module 1 operation, including raw materials used, production campaigns, process parameters, batches obtained, controls performed and relevant incidents. PP will validate that batch identification is maintained during downstream transformation in Module 2, ensuring continuity between recycled material batches and board/material production. CABKA will provide input on the identification needs of the recovered polyolefin streams intended for reusable packaging and logistics validation in Module 3. ITENE will link batch identification data with the characterisation and quality control results generated in T3.4, ensuring that each released batch can be associated with its technical evidence. EDRO and MUN will contribute requirements from the future validation environments, ensuring that product and batch identification can support deployment, use, return, maintenance and acceptance assessment in the WP5 demonstrators.
The task will follow a progressive approach: first defining the identification model and critical data fields, then consolidating production records from the pre-industrial campaigns, checking data quality and consistency, and finally preparing the transfer of structured information to WP4. This will ensure that all relevant material, batch, process and quality information is available before the closed-loop traceability architecture is implemented. By the end of the task, the consortium will have a validated pre-industrial batch identification protocol and a consolidated production information package ready to be integrated into the digital traceability framework. This will support continuity between material production, product manufacturing, demonstration, return-loop monitoring and circularity verification. The results of this task will support MS8 and will be reported in D3.4.

wps.title_source_en: Work Package 4: Return-Ciclo management, digital traceability and circularity verification
wps.title_es: Espacio de datos conjunto, trazabilidad integral, retorno y aseguramiento de circularidad
wps.objective_source_en:
WP4 will design, structure and validate the operational and digital framework required to close and verify the R-Mob TraceLoop circular value chains. It will ensure that waste streams, material batches, transformation processes, products, use phases, return events and reintegration routes can be identified, traced and verified through a governed espacio de datos architecture. Its specific objectives are to:
Define the return-Ciclo operating models and application-specific protocols for the furniture/equipment, construction/municipal infrastructure and reusable embalaje ciclos.
Transform the technical evidence generated in WP2 and WP3 into auditable data assets connected to physical and digital identifiers.
Design the digital traceability architecture, data model, governance rules and ODRL policy framework needed for controlled data exchange between value-chain actors.
Develop a Digital Product Passport prototype linking material origin, recycled content, transformation history, quality evidence, use conditions, return events and end-of-life or reintegration routes.
Establish a dynamic circularity verification approach based on events, evidence and conformity rules rather than static documentary traceability.
Prepare the protocols, templates, acceptance criteria and data collection tools required to validate the traceability and return-Ciclo systems during the WP5 demonstrations.
Ensure that the traceability framework provides reliable evidence for WP6 impact assessment and supports exploitation, certification and replication activities in WP7.
WP4 will deliver the operational and digital backbone of the R-Mob TraceLoop ecosystem. The work package will produce the return-Ciclo protocols, espacio de datos architecture, traceability data model, governance framework, ODRL policy library, Digital Product Passport prototype and circularity verification methodology needed to connect physical assets with trusted data assets. By the end of the WP, each relevant waste stream, material batch, transformed material and demonstrator product will be linked to a unique identification logic and a sequence of traceable events, enabling chain-of-custody reconstruction, controlled data sharing, circularity declaraciones verification and preparación for real-environment validation in WP5.
wps.objective_es:
WP4 diseñará, implementará y dejará preparado para validación el espacio de datos conjunto R-Mob TraceLoop, tomando como núcleo la capacidad preexistente de EDRO para producto, activo y operación y federándola con la información de residuo, materia, transformación, lote, calidad, ensayos y ACV generada por los socios. La arquitectura cubrirá sin discontinuidades la cadena completa: origen del residuo, caracterización, lote de materia, transformación, placa o material, familia de producto, unidad identificada y DPP, instalación y POI, uso, mantenimiento, retorno, reutilización o reintegración y segundo ciclo.

EDRO liderará el modelo canónico, la arquitectura de federación, las correspondencias semánticas, los identificadores de enlace, los productos de datos y APIs, la incorporación de familias, productos, activos, lectores y dispositivos, y la gobernanza operacional. ITENE aportará y validará la evidencia técnica de materia y proceso. KIWA desarrollará RegFlow Audit, las reglas de declaración-evidencia, las puertas de conformidad, la trazabilidad de auditoría y las condiciones de aseguramiento e intercambio. Ningún componente de aseguramiento creará identidades, DPP, modelos de producto o registros operativos paralelos.

El paquete entregará protocolos de retorno ejecutables; arquitectura y modelo de datos conjunto; perfiles DPP/POI; reglas de incorporación de fuentes y socios; catálogo de productos de datos; interfaces controladas; RegFlow Audit; biblioteca de políticas; y un paquete de puesta en servicio para los demostradores WP5.

EDRO; Participants: CABKA, KIWA, MANC, MUN) (M9-M13):
This task will define the operational return protocols for the project applications, ensuring that products manufactured with valorised materials can be inspected, maintained, reused, returned and reintegrated into the circular value chain under clear technical criteria and verifiable data requirements. The task will translate the closed-loop design principles defined in WP2 into practical return procedures to be tested during the WP5 demonstrations.
EDRO will lead the functional definition of the return protocols, considering the real use conditions. The work will first map the expected return scenarios, actors and responsibilities, including product possession, use, maintenance, collection, transfer of custody, return by incident, ordinary return and end-of-life routes. MUN will contribute the municipal/end-user perspective, including public-space use conditions, maintenance needs, acceptance requirements and operational constraints for deployment and return. The task will then define the inspection, classification and acceptance criteria for returned products and materials. This will include visual, technical and functional inspection rules; classification of product condition; criteria for acceptance, rejection, repair, reuse or reprocessing; and identification of damage, contamination, loss of functionality or safety restrictions. MANC will contribute criteria related to reception, preparation and potential reprocessing of returned materials, ensuring that reintegration routes remain technically feasible. CABKA will provide specific requirements for reusable packaging, including return handling, pool management, reuse cycles and operational acceptance of recovered products. KIWA will integrate the return protocols into the traceability and verification logic of WP4. This will include defining the return-related events to be captured, the minimum evidence required for each operational decision, the datasets to be linked to the Digital Product Passport, and the records needed to support dynamic circularity verification. Return events such as use, maintenance, transfer, inspection, repair, reuse and reintegration will be connected to the Data Space data model and to the circularity claims to be validated later in the project.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have application-specific return protocols defining responsibilities, inspection criteria, maintenance and reuse routes, acceptance rules, reintegration options and minimum data requirements for each closed loop. These protocols will provide the operational basis for the WP5 and the data requirements for the WP4 traceability architecture. The results of this task will support MS9 and will feed D4.1

tasks.heading_source_en: T.4.2 Digital traceability architecture and data model (Leader:
tasks.heading_es: T.4.2 Arquitectura digital de trazabilidad y modelo de datos (Asunto:
tasks.source_en:
KIWA; Participants: EDRO, ITENE, MANC, PP) (M7-M13):
This task will design the digital traceability architecture and data model of LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop, ensuring that all critical events across the waste–material–product–use–return chain can be registered as interoperable, auditable and reusable data assets within a governed Data Space. The objective is to avoid static documentary traceability and enable evidence-based verification of circularity, recycled content, chain of custody and material suitability.
KIWA will lead the definition of the traceability architecture, including the digital entities, event taxonomy, identifiers, relationships, evidence model and data quality rules. The work will first define the traceability requirements and the minimum certifiable perimeter, identifying which processes, materials, batches, products and return events must be traced. It will map the data sources generated in WP2, WP3, WP4, WP5 and WP6, and will define the circularity claims that must be supported by verifiable evidence. KIWA will also define the Data Space logic, including data products, partner-specific catalogues, digital identities, access permissions, transaction records and conceptual interfaces with connectors or APIs. MANC and PP will provide process, production, batch and transformation data, including the relationship between recycled material batches and downstream products. ITENE will contribute characterisation variables, test results, technical criteria and material quality data, ensuring that the traceability model can incorporate scientific and technical evidence. EDRO will validate that the data model reflects real product use, deployment and return conditions, particularly for construction, municipal infrastructure and operational closed-loop applications.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have a frozen traceability architecture and data model ready to support the DPP prototype, return-loop validation and RegFlow Audit protocol. The task will provide the digital backbone required to transform physical materials and products into trusted data assets. The task will then develop the semantic data model, covering entities such as waste stream, material batch, processing event, quality test, product unit, return event and reintegration route. It will define how waste fractions, production batches, transformation processes, product units, DPP and return-loop events are connected. Critical fields such as origin, date, mass, composition, contaminants, process parameters, test results, responsible actor and conformity status will be normalised to ensure consistency and comparability across partners. The architecture will be prepared for integration with the DPP and for use during WP5 demonstrations. Data quality, lineage and verifiability rules will be established, including completeness, consistency, temporality and uniqueness criteria, as well as automatic checks and manual review points where needed. The results of this task will support MS10 and will feed D4.2.

tasks.source_en:
KIWA; Participants: EDRO, ITENE, MANC, PP) (M10-M14):
This task will develop the physical and digital identification model for products and material batches, together with a Digital Product Passport prototype able to provide authorised access to critical information on material origin, composition, transformation, quality, use, maintenance, return and circularity. The task will connect the project’s physical assets with their digital records, ensuring that demonstrator products can be traced and verified throughout their lifecycle.
KIWA will lead the specification of the identification model and DPP structure, defining how physical identifiers, material batches, production processes, quality evidence and circularity claims will be linked. The task will assess suitable identification technologies, such as QR codes, RFID, digital labels, tags or equivalent solutions, considering durability, readability, cost, ease of implementation, compatibility with use conditions and recyclability. Unique identifiers will be defined for relevant batches, products, components and return events. KIWA will develop a functional DPP prototype for representative products or batches and connect it conceptually with the Data Space catalogue, event model and access policies defined in T4.2. The prototype will be tested with selected cases to verify the linkage between batch, product and DPP, as well as reading, consultation, update and access control functionalities. Adjustments will be introduced before the system is used in the WP5 demonstrations. MANC and PP will provide the batch, production and transformation data needed to feed the passport and ensure continuity between recycled materials and products. ITENE will contribute characterisation, quality control and technical conformity data, ensuring that material performance evidence is included in the DPP. EDRO will provide product-level requirements, use conditions and return-related consultation needs, ensuring that the DPP is useful for real operational environments and future WP5 validation.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have a defined physical and digital identification model, a functional DPP prototype and a validated linkage between products, batches, technical data and circularity claims. The work will then define the content model of the DPP, including mandatory and optional data fields related to origin, composition, processing history, quality results, application, use, maintenance, return and reintegration. Access levels will be established for different user profiles, including producers, transformers, verifiers, users, municipalities and return managers. Each data field will be linked to its source, date, responsible actor and level of confidence, ensuring that the DPP supports verifiable and auditable information rather than generic product claims. The results of this task will support MS11 and identification workflow ready and will be reported in D4.3.

tasks.heading_source_en: T.4.4 Circularity verification and RegFlow Audit protocol (Leader:
tasks.heading_es: T.4.4.4 Verificación de Circularidad y protocolo de auditoría de RegFlow (Asuntos:
tasks.source_en:
KIWA; Participants: EDRO, ITENE, MANC,) (M12-M16):
This task will develop the circularity verification and RegFlow Audit protocol of LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop, enabling a dynamic, data-based audit of traceability, conformity, material quality, recycled content, chain of custody and effective loop closure for the project demonstrators. The objective is to transform technical and operational data into auditable evidence supporting reliable circularity claims.
KIWA will lead the definition of the verification framework, including the claims to be verified, conformity criteria, evidence requirements, decision rules and certification logic. The protocol will cover key claims such as waste origin, material composition, recycled content, applied valorisation process, batch quality, suitability for application, use, return and reintegration. It will define acceptance, deviation and non-conformity criteria, ensuring alignment with the technical requirements established in WP2, the production and quality evidence generated in WP3, and the validation needs of WP5. KIWA will design the RegFlow Audit workflow by connecting regulatory requirements, process flows and data flows. The workflow will define event-based audit points covering waste input, valorisation, batch production, quality control, product manufacturing, use, maintenance, return and reintegration. It will also establish conformity gates before materials or products move from one phase to the next, using the DPP as a consultation interface and the Data Space as the source of evidence. MANC will provide process, production, operation and chain-of-custody evidence from the valorisation system and batch production activities. ITENE will contribute technical criteria, characterisation results and testing evidence to support material conformity and quality claims. EDRO will validate the applicability of the protocol to real product use, return and reintegration scenarios, ensuring that the audit approach can be applied under WP5 demonstration conditions.
The protocol will be piloted on representative batches and products to verify data availability, sufficiency of evidence and readiness for real-environment validation. Any evidence gaps or operational inconsistencies identified before WP5 will be documented and corrected through updated rules, templates or data requirements. The task will then establish an evidence matrix indicating which data are required for each claim and each stage of the value chain, who is responsible for generating and validating them, and how they must be stored, accessed and audited. Decision rules will be defined to classify claims or process steps as validated, conditional, pending, rejected or requiring additional sampling. Data quality, lineage and audit trail requirements will be incorporated to ensure that the verification process is transparent and reproducible. The circularity verification approach will take into account UNE-EN 15343 principles for recycled plastics traceability and recycled content assessment, defining how evidence is recorded and linked across the chain from waste input and recycled raw material to formulation, transformed product and final application. By the end of the task, the consortium will have a circularity verification protocol, evidence matrix, decision rules and RegFlow Audit workflow ready to support dynamic certification and traceability-based validation during the WP5 demonstrations. The results of this task will contribute to MS12 and will feed D4.4.
tasks.source_es:

Definirá declaraciones verificables, reglas de correspondencia declaración-evidencia, puertas de conformidad, tolerancias, tratamiento de ausencia o contradicción de datos, muestreo, revisión humana, trazabilidad de auditoría y preparación para certificación. Las reglas podrán verificar origen, contenido reciclado, cadena de custodia, calidad, aptitud, reutilización, retorno e integridad de la trazabilidad.

EDRO habilitará interfaces de solo lectura o productos de datos controlados desde DPP/POI, eventos operativos, stock y retorno; ITENE aportará resultados y criterios técnicos; los productores aportarán los registros de origen y proceso. RegFlow registrará qué evidencia fue consultada, qué regla se aplicó, su versión, el resultado y la justificación. KIWA no emitirá identificadores, no administrará DPP ni POI, no modificará estados de producto o activo y no sustituirá la gobernanza de fuente. La salida será una metodología reproducible, una biblioteca versionada de reglas y un expediente de auditoría utilizable en WP5, WP6 y WP7.

EDRO; Participants: ITENE, KIWA, MANC, PP) (M15-M18):
This task will consolidate all operational, digital and verification elements required to start the WP5 demonstrations under a common validation readiness package. It will ensure that demonstrator products, material batches, identifiers, return protocols, DPP elements, data capture templates and audit rules are prepared before deployment in real or controlled operational environments.
EDRO will lead the operational preparation of the validation package, defining the readiness criteria for each closed loop and ensuring that the protocols are adapted to the expected use conditions of furniture/public equipment, construction or municipal infrastructure, and reusable packaging/logistics applications. The task will act as the transition gate between the design and verification activities of WP4 and the real-environment demonstrations of WP5. KIWA will verify that the package includes the traceability, DPP, data, evidence and control requirements needed to apply the dynamic circularity verification approach during the demonstrations. This will include the review of product identifiers, batch data, return-event records, audit templates, access rules, evidence requirements and RegFlow Audit decision points. ITENE will confirm that the technical quality criteria, material characterisation data and conformity evidence from WP3 are available and can be used during validation. MANC and PP will provide the production, batch and transformation information needed to prepare the demonstrators for deployment, ensuring continuity between pre-industrial production, product manufacturing and validation. The task will integrate the return protocols, DPP prototype, data policies and RegFlow Audit rules into application-specific validation packages, adapted to each closed loop and its indicators, evidence needs and operational control points.
The work will include the definition of readiness checklists, minimum data and evidence requirements, deployment start conditions, stop criteria, responsibilities during validation, data capture templates and corrective action procedures. A joint technical review will be carried out before the start of WP5 to confirm the availability of products, data, identifiers, protocols and verification tools, and to identify any remaining gaps or corrective actions. By the end of the task, the consortium will have a consolidated WP5 validation readiness package, including checklists, templates, responsibilities, DPP/identifier requirements and audit evidence structures for each closed loop. This package will be formally transferred to WP5 as the operational basis for the demonstration phase. The results of this task will contribute to MS12 and will be included in D4.4

tasks.heading_source_en: T.4.6 Data governance framework and ODRL policy library (Leader:
tasks.heading_es: T.4.6 Marco de gobernanza de datos y biblioteca de políticas de la ODRL (Asuntos:
tasks.source_en:
KIWA; Participants: EDRO, ITENE, MANC, MUN) (M8-M13):
This task will define the data governance framework of the R-Mob TraceLoop Data Space and develop an ODRL policy library regulating access, use, reuse, purpose, retention and auditability of the data required for traceability and circularity verification. The objective is to enable controlled data sharing between partners while preserving data sovereignty, confidentiality and proportionality according to the sensitivity of each dataset.
KIWA will lead the definition of the governance model, including data owners, data providers, data consumers, verifiers and operators, as well as their responsibilities for data capture, validation, custody, updating and auditability. The task will classify project data according to sensitivity, criticality and relevance for verification, applying data minimisation and proportionality principles so that only the information required for traceability, DPP operation and RegFlow Audit is shared. KIWA will also define the data quality, trust and auditability criteria required for the dynamic certification model, including completeness, consistency, timeliness, traceability, accuracy, access logs, version control, corrections and lineage evidence. The governance framework will be aligned with the data model defined in T4.2, the DPP prototype developed in T4.3 and the RegFlow Audit protocol of T4.4, ensuring that data availability and access conditions are compatible with WP5 validation needs. MANC and ITENE will define the restrictions, availability and sensitivity of industrial, production, process, characterisation and quality data. EDRO will contribute access and use requirements linked to products, users, deployment conditions and return events. MUN will provide the municipal/end-user perspective where applicable, including restrictions related to access, treatment or publication of data generated in public or municipal demonstration scenarios.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have a validated data governance framework, a reusable ODRL policy library, and clear rules for data quality, lineage, access control and auditability across the R-Mob TraceLoop Data Space. The task will then develop a reusable ODRL policy library for the main project data exchange scenarios. These policies will define access rights by role, purpose and dataset, including permissions, prohibitions and obligations related to use, non-redistribution, retention, aggregation, exploitation and audit access. The policy library will be designed to support the traceability architecture, DPP consultation and circularity verification activities without exposing unnecessary industrial, technical or commercially sensitive information. The results of this task will support MS12 and will feed D4.3.

wps.title_es: Implantación y validación en entorno real de demostradores de ciclo cerrado
wps.objective_source_en:
WP5 will implement and validate the R-Mob TraceLoop closed-Ciclo demonstrators under real or representative operating conditions, using the materials, protocols and traceability tools developed in WP2, WP3 and WP4. Its specific objectives are to:
Manufacture, deploy and validate demonstrators for the three project closed ciclos: furniture (DEMO1), construction (DEMO2) and embalaje (DEMO3).
Demonstrate the technical and functional suitability of recycled materials produced through the R-Mob TraceLoop valorisation system in real application contexts.
Validate the operational feasibility of the return-Ciclo protocols, including use, maintenance, inspection, return, reuse, repair, recovery and reintegration routes.
Test the traceability, product identification and DPP elements during demonstrator deployment and use.
Generate harmonised operational data on performance, durability, user acceptance, logistics, return rates, reuse cycles, traceability completeness and operational barriers.
Provide validated evidence for WP6 impact assessment and WP7 exploitation, replication and post-LIFE market uptake activities.
WP5 will deliver three validated closed-Ciclo demonstrators. The work package will generate real-environment evidence on material performance, product functionality, durability, maintenance, user or municipal acceptance, logistics behaviour, return feasibility and traceability operation. By the end of the WP, the project will have demonstrated the practical applicability of the R-Mob TraceLoop circular model, produced the evidence required for impact assessment and certification inputs, and identified the main operational conditions for replication and market uptake.
wps.objective_es:
WP5 implementará y validará los demostradores de la R-Mob TraceLoop en condiciones de funcionamiento reales o representativas, utilizando los materiales, protocolos y herramientas de trazabilidad desarrolladas en WP2, WP3 y WP4. Sus objetivos específicos son: Fabricación, despliegue y validación de los demostradores para los tres circuitos cerrados del proyecto: mobiliario (DEMO1), construcción (DEMO2) y embalaje (DEMO3).
Demostrar la idoneidad técnica y funcional de los materiales reciclados producidos a través del sistema de valorización R-Mob TraceLoop en contextos de aplicación reales. Validar la viabilidad operacional de los protocolos de retorno, incluyendo el uso, mantenimiento, inspección, retorno, reutilización, reparación, recuperación y rutas de reintegración.
Probar la trazabilidad, identificación de productos y elementos DPP durante el despliegue y uso de demostradores. Generar datos operativos armonizados sobre rendimiento, durabilidad, aceptación de usuarios, logística, tasas de retorno, ciclos de reutilización, integridad de trazabilidad y barreras operacionales. Proporcionar pruebas validadas para la evaluación de impacto WP6 y la explotación, replicación y actividades de captación de mercado después de LIFE.
WP5 entregará tres demostradores validados de ciclo cerrado. El paquete de trabajo generará evidencia real sobre el rendimiento material, funcionalidad de producto, durabilidad, mantenimiento, aceptación de usuario o municipal, comportamiento logístico, viabilidad de retorno y operación de trazabilidad.
Al final del WP, el proyecto habrá demostrado la aplicabilidad práctica del modelo circular R-Mob TraceLoop, producido las pruebas necesarias para la evaluación de impactos y los insumos de certificación, e identificado las principales condiciones operacionales para la replicación y la captación de mercado.

Circular furniture and public/interior equipment validation (Leader: MANC; Participants: ITENE, MUN, PP) (M18-M27):
This task will implement and validate the first circular loop of the project through the manufacturing, installation and monitoring of furniture and public/interior equipment solutions produced from recycled boards obtained from complex plastic waste streams. The task will demonstrate the technical and functional feasibility of the products developed in the project, as well as the operation of the circular model during the use phase, including traceability, user acceptance, maintenance needs and end-of-life recovery potential.
MANC will lead the task and coordinate the planning, technical development, manufacturing, installation and validation of the DEMO1. A total of XXX furniture sets will be produced and installed in XXX municipal, public or interior validation sites, to be confirmed with the participating municipality/end user. The demonstrators will be selected to represent realistic use cases with replication potential in public spaces, municipal facilities, offices, schools, cultural buildings or other controlled environments. MANC will define the product specifications and coordinate the transformation of the recycled materials produced in WP3 into final demonstrator solutions. PP will manufacture the recycled boards and perform the CNC machining, cutting, milling and finishing operations required to obtain the designed components. MANC will then carry out the final assembly, mounting and preparation of the products before deployment. During the validation period, MANC will monitor the technical performance of the products, including functionality, mechanical behaviour, durability, maintenance needs, incidents and recovery potential. Once manufactured, the demonstrators will be transported and installed at the selected validation sites with the support of MUN. The municipality/end user will provide the installation spaces, coordinate access and operational conditions, support interaction with final users and contribute to the assessment of acceptance, usability, maintenance and green public procurement potential. Initial checks will confirm correct installation, functionality, safety of use and registration of product identification and traceability information. ITENE will define and support the technical monitoring methodology, collect relevant data for WP6 impact assessment and contribute to the interpretation of results. Traceability information will be recorded during deployment and use, including product identification, location, use conditions, maintenance events and potential return/end-of-life scenarios, ensuring coherence with the WP4 validation readiness package.
The task will conclude with the consolidation of demonstration results, including technical and functional performance, user and municipal feedback, operational barriers, maintenance needs, traceability completeness, green public procurement potential and recommendations for future implementation. The results will feed WP6 impact assessment and WP7 exploitation, replication and after-LIFE uptake activities. By the end of the task, the consortium will have manufactured, installed and validated the Closed Loop 1 demonstrators in real or representative use conditions, generating evidence on the applicability of recycled board-based solutions for circular furniture and public/interior equipment. The results of this task will support MS13 and will be reported in D5.1.
tasks.source_es:
Validación de mobiliario circular y equipo público/interior (Líder: MANC; Participantes: ITENE, MUN, PP) (M18-M27):
Esta tarea implementará y validará el primer ciclo circular del proyecto mediante la fabricación, instalación y seguimiento de mobiliario y soluciones de equipamiento público/interior producidas a partir de tablas recicladas obtenidas a partir de corrientes complejas de residuos plásticos.
La tarea demostrará la viabilidad técnica y funcional de los productos desarrollados en el proyecto, así como el funcionamiento del modelo circular durante la fase de uso, incluyendo trazabilidad, aceptación de los usuarios, necesidades de mantenimiento y potencial de recuperación final de LIFE.
MANC dirigirá la tarea y coordinará la planificación, desarrollo técnico, fabricación, instalación y validación de la DEMO1. Se producirá e instalará un total de XXX conjuntos de muebles en XXX locales municipales, públicos o de validación interior, que se confirmarán con el usuario municipal/final participante.
Los demostradores serán seleccionados para representar casos de uso realista con potencial de replicación en espacios públicos, instalaciones municipales, oficinas, escuelas, edificios culturales u otros entornos controlados. MANC definirá las especificaciones del producto y coordinará la transformación de los materiales reciclados producidos en WP3 en soluciones de demostración definitivas.
PP fabricará las tablas recicladas y realizará las operaciones de mecanizado, corte, fresado y acabado CNC necesarias para obtener los componentes diseñados. MANC realizará la instalación final, montaje y preparación de los productos antes del despliegue.
Durante el período de validación, MANC supervisará el rendimiento técnico de los productos, incluyendo funcionalidad, comportamiento mecánico, durabilidad, necesidades de mantenimiento, incidentes y potencial de recuperación. Una vez fabricados, los demostradores serán transportados e instalados en los sitios de validación seleccionados con el apoyo de MUN.
El usuario municipal/fin proporcionará los espacios de instalación, coordinará el acceso y las condiciones operacionales, apoyará la interacción con los usuarios finales y contribuirá a evaluar la aceptación, usabilidad, mantenimiento y potencial de contratación pública verde. Los cheques iniciales confirmarán la instalación correcta, funcionalidad, seguridad de uso e registro de información de identificación y trazabilidad de productos.
ITENE definirá y apoyará la metodología de seguimiento técnico, recopilará datos relevantes para la evaluación de impactos WP6 y contribuirá a la interpretación de resultados. La información de rastreabilidad se registrará durante el despliegue y uso, incluyendo identificación de productos, ubicación, condiciones de uso, eventos de mantenimiento y posibles escenarios de retorno/fin de LIFE, asegurando coherencia con el paquete de validación WP4.
La tarea concluirá con la consolidación de los resultados de demostración, incluidos los resultados técnicos y funcionales, la retroalimentación de los usuarios y municipales, las barreras operacionales, las necesidades de mantenimiento, la integridad de la trazabilidad, el potencial de contratación pública verde y las recomendaciones para la futura implementación. Los resultados serán el alimento para la evaluación de impacto de WP6 y la explotación, replicación y actividades posteriores a LIFE.
Al final de la tarea, el consorcio habrá fabricado, instalado y validado los demostradores de Cerrada Ciclo 1 en condiciones reales o representativas de uso, generando evidencia sobre la aplicabilidad de soluciones basadas en tableros reciclados para muebles circulares y equipo público/interior. Los resultados de esta tarea serán compatibles con MS13 y se informarán en D5.1.

Construction and municipal infrastructure validation (Leader: EDRO; Participants: ITENE, MANC, MUN, PP) (M18-M27):
This task will implement and validate the second circular loop of the project through the manufacturing, installation and monitoring of construction-oriented and/or municipal infrastructure demonstrators produced from recycled boards obtained from complex plastic waste streams. The task will demonstrate the technical, operational and functional feasibility of using R-Mob TraceLoop recycled materials in real or representative built-environment applications, assessing their performance, durability, maintenance needs, traceability and potential for replication in municipal or private infrastructure contexts.
EDRO will lead the task and planning, technical development, manufacturing, installation and validation of the DEMO2. A total of XXX paving tiles for cycling lanes will be produced and installed in XXX validation sites, to be confirmed with the participating municipality, infrastructure owner or private end user. EDRO will ensure that the demonstrator design is compatible with real construction or municipal infrastructure conditions, including installation constraints, use environment, maintenance requirements, safety considerations, acceptance criteria and future recovery routes. MUN will contribute the end-user and municipal perspective, supporting the selection of sites, access conditions, deployment feasibility and validation of public or operational acceptance. MANC will provide the recycled material inputs produced through the advanced valorisation system and will support the technical adaptation of the materials to the target applications. PP will manufacture the recycled boards in the WP3 and carry out the required machining, cutting, finishing or preparation steps for their use in the demonstrators. EDRO will coordinate the final preparation and installation of the demonstrators, ensuring that deployment is carried out according to the validation plan and that traceability identifiers and product-related information are properly registered.
During the validation period, EDRO will monitor the operational performance of the demonstrators, including functionality, installation behaviour, durability, maintenance needs, incidents, resistance to use conditions, recovery feasibility and barriers to adoption in construction or municipal infrastructure environments. Traceability data will be recorded throughout deployment and use, including product identification, location, installation conditions, maintenance events and potential return or reintegration options, in line with the WP4 validation readiness package.
The task will conclude with the consolidation of the validation results, including technical and operational performance, municipal or end-user feedback, installation and maintenance lessons, traceability completeness, regulatory or procurement-related considerations, and recommendations for replication in other construction or municipal infrastructure contexts. The results will feed WP6 impact assessment and WP7 exploitation, replication and after-LIFE uptake activities.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have manufactured, installed and validated the Closed Loop 2 demonstrators in real or representative built-environment conditions, generating evidence on the applicability of recycled board/panel solutions for circular construction and municipal infrastructure applications. The results of this task will support MS13 and will be reported in D5.2.

KIWA; Participants: CEV, EDRO, ITENE, MANC, PP) (M18-M29):
This task will coordinate the harmonised monitoring and data collection activities across the three closed-loop demonstrations implemented in WP5. The objective is to ensure that comparable operational, circularity, traceability, certification-related and market-relevant data are collected from all demonstrators and can be used as reliable evidence for WP6 impact assessment, WP7 exploitation and replication activities, and LIFE reporting.
KIWA will lead the task, ensuring that the data collected during the demonstrations are aligned with the traceability architecture, Digital Product Passport and RegFlow Audit requirements defined in WP4. This will include verifying the completeness and consistency of product identifiers, batch-product links, deployment records, maintenance events, return events, reuse cycles, circularity evidence and certification inputs. KIWA will also coordinate the evidence structure required to support recycled content, reuse, return-loop performance and traceability-based verification claims. ITENE will support the definition of the monitoring methodology and the technical and environmental data collection framework, ensuring that the information gathered from the demonstrations can feed WP6 impact assessment. The monitoring framework will cover product units deployed, material volumes, recycled content, use conditions, performance results, incidents, maintenance operations, repairs, reuse cycles, returns, traceability records, user feedback and operational barriers.MANC will provide operational data from the furniture/public equipment loop, including product deployment, use performance, maintenance needs, traceability records and recovery feasibility. EDRO will provide data from the construction and municipal infrastructure loop, focusing on installation conditions, functionality, durability, operational constraints, acceptance and return potential. PP will contribute information related to material transformation, board production and product manufacturing, ensuring continuity between material batches and final demonstrators. CEV will contribute to the collection and interpretation of market, user, buyer and adoption-related feedback, including acceptance by public or private end users, green public procurement potential and barriers to uptake.
The validation evidence collected during the demonstrators will support future certification or verification processes, including alignment with UNE-EN 15343 where applicable, by documenting the continuity of traceability and recycled content information across successive transformation steps, from waste input to final product.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have a consolidated cross-loop dataset and operational evidence package covering the technical, functional, circularity, traceability and acceptance performance of the three demonstrations. These results will provide the basis for WP6 impact evaluation and WP7 replication, exploitation and after-LIFE market uptake activities. They will support MS14 and will feed D5.4

wps.title_source_en: Work Package 6: Performance assessment, KPI seguimiento and impact validation
wps.title_es: Evaluación del rendimiento, seguimiento de KPI y validación de impacto
wps.objective_source_en:
WP6 will monitor, evaluate and validate the overall performance of LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop, verifying the achievement of the technical, environmental, economic, circularity and market objectives established in the proposal. Its specific objectives are to:
Monitor the project’s KPIs throughout implementation, building on the baseline and KPI framework defined in WP2.
Assess circularity and resource efficiency performance, including waste valorised, recycled content, virgin material substitution, return rates, reuse cycles and reintegration into the value chain.
Evaluate the environmental performance of the materials, products and closed-Ciclo systems through carbon footprint, GHG reduction, energy savings and ACV/PEF-aligned analysis.
Assess the technical and operational performance of the valorisation system, recycled materials and WP5 demonstrators, including quality, durability, functionality, logistics, traceability completeness and operational barriers.
Analyse techno-economic, socio-economic and market performance, including cost competitiveness, scalability, employment generation, user/municipal acceptance, green public procurement potential and Close2Market indicators.
Consolidate data from WP2, WP3, WP4 and WP5 to provide objective evidence for LIFE elaboración de informes, the post-LIFE strategy, exploitation and replication activities.
WP6 will deliver a consolidated and evidence-based assessment of the project’s impacts, comparing baseline values, project-end results and post-LIFE projections. The work package will generate validated indicators on circularity, environmental performance, technical and operational feasibility, socio-economic benefits and market potential. It will provide the quantitative evidence needed to demonstrate the contribution of R-Mob TraceLoop to resource efficiency, waste valorisation, recycled material uptake, closed-Ciclo implementation and future replication, while supporting LIFE elaboración de informes, exploitation planning and the post-LIFE sustainability model.
wps.objective_es:
WP6 supervisará, evaluará y validará el desempeño general de LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop, verificando el logro de los objetivos técnicos, ambientales, económicos, circularidad y de mercado establecidos en la propuesta. Sus objetivos específicos son: Supervisar los KPI del proyecto durante toda la implementación, basándose en el marco de referencia y KPI definido en WP2.
Evaluar el rendimiento de la circularidad y la eficiencia de los recursos, incluidos los contenidos valorados, reciclados, sustitución de materiales vírgenes, tasas de retorno, ciclos de reutilización y reintegración en la cadena de valor. Evaluar el rendimiento ambiental de los materiales, productos y sistemas de ciclo cerrado mediante huella de carbono, reducción de GEI, ahorro energético y análisis alineados con ACV/PEF.
Evaluar el rendimiento técnico y operacional del sistema de valorización, materiales reciclados y demostradores WP5, incluyendo calidad, durabilidad, funcionalidad, logística, integridad de trazabilidad y barreras operativas.
Analizar el rendimiento tecnológico, socioeconómico y de mercado, incluyendo competitividad de costes, escalabilidad, generación de empleo, aceptación de usuario/municipal, potencial de contratación pública verde y indicadores de Close2Market. Consolidar datos de WP2, WP3, WP4 y WP5 para proporcionar evidencia objetiva para la presentación de informes de LIFE, la estrategia de post-LIFE, actividades de explotación y replicación.
WP6 realizará una evaluación consolidada y basada en pruebas de los impactos del proyecto, comparando valores de referencia, resultados de proyecto y proyecciones posteriores a LIFE. El paquete de trabajo generará indicadores validados sobre la circularidad, el rendimiento ambiental, viabilidad técnica y operacional, beneficios socioeconómicos y potencial de mercado.
Proporcionará las pruebas cuantitativas necesarias para demostrar la contribución de R-Mob TraceLoop a la eficiencia de los recursos, la valorización de los residuos, la captación de material reciclado, la implementación de cierres cerrados y la replicación futura, al tiempo que apoyará la presentación de informes de LIFE, la planificación de la explotación y el modelo de sostenibilidad post-LIFE.

tasks.heading_source_en: T.6.1 Circularity and resource efficiency performance (Leader:
tasks.heading_es: T.6.1 Circularidad y rendimiento de la eficiencia de los recursos (Asuntos:
tasks.source_en:
MANC; Participants: ITENE, KIWA, UVIGO) (M3-M32):
This task will monitor and evaluate the circularity and resource efficiency performance achieved by LIFE R-Mob TraceLoop. It will quantify the project’s contribution to waste valorisation, recycled content, substitution of virgin raw materials, resource efficiency, return rates, reuse cycles and reintegration of materials into the value chain, providing a consistent evidence base for the overall impact assessment.
MANC will lead the task and coordinate the definition and implementation of the circularity monitoring framework. The work will build on the baseline and KPI framework established in WP2 and will define the indicators, data sources, calculation methods, reporting frequency and responsibilities needed to track circularity performance throughout the project. The task will also compare the results achieved by each solution with the baseline and expected targets, identifying deviations or improvement opportunities when needed. The monitoring will cover the main circularity indicators linked to the project’s technical activities and demonstrations, including amounts of complex plastic waste valorised, recycled material incorporated into new products, reduction in virgin material use, production efficiency, material losses, product return rates, reuse cycles and reintegration routes. In addition to these specific indicators, the task will assess the overall circularity level of each solution using aggregated metrics inspired by recognised circularity frameworks, such as Circulytics, adapted to the project context. ITENE and UVIGO will support the methodological definition of the indicators, validate the technical consistency of the results and use the collected data as input for the environmental assessment in T6.2. KIWA will provide verified traceability data from the digital layer developed in WP4 and validated in WP5, checking the consistency, quality and auditability of the information used to calculate circularity indicators. This will ensure that circularity performance is based on traceable and verifiable evidence rather than only on manual estimates. Recycled content and circularity indicators will be calculated using traceable evidence generated along the value chain and, where applicable, aligned with UNE-EN 15343 principles to strengthen the credibility of project claims and support future verification or certification processes.
By the end of the task, the consortium will have implemented a circularity monitoring system, validated the baseline for circularity assessment, monitored the evolution of circularity indicators during the project and consolidated the information required for the environmental, economic and final LIFE KPI evaluation. The results of this task will contribute to MS16 and will feed D6.1.
